physical: Interaction with an environment spreads a system's phase relations into degrees of freedom no one can recover, suppressing interference; two branches of a superposition lose coherence faster the more strongly they couple to the environment and the farther apart in position they are.
reflected_sentence: With receptivity, keeping what was together becomes easier rather than harder.
rule_reason: The single coherence cost explicitly includes separation made by distance, so the reading turns around. Environment coupling is explicitly not resistance and does not add another qualifying cost.
closing: The supplied separation feature forces turns around. Calling coupling resistance would contradict the fixed assignments, and calling decoherence Culmination would invent a mapping. The missing partners prevent a frozen formula or interpretation, so those fields are empty.
